modern_card.name: Brionac, Dragon of the Ice Barrier

review.notes:
Chain starts at v3 (H5SE-EN001, 2012-03-30), the version the baseline best matches. Earlier transitions v0 (HA01-EN022, 2009-11-05) -> v1 (undated) -> v2 (DT01-EN031, 2010-01-29) -> v3 are PSCT rewordings ('discard any number of cards to return the same number of cards from the field to the hand' -> 'discard ... to target the same number of cards on the field; return those targets to the hand') that formalise targeting without changing resolution; the Edison-era printing is v2 and behaves as the baseline implements. Trailing v4 -> v5 (DUDE-EN008, 2019-10-10) is the Graveyard/GY rewording, cosmetic, not recorded. Minor note: the variant's cdb text ('You can discard any number of cards, then target an equal number of cards on the field; return them to the hand.') is upstream's own paraphrase rather than any printed version (closest v3, ratio 0.8397), though it states the same behaviour as v2/v3. Card data identical to modern (2300/1400, Level 6, WATER, Sea Serpent, Synchro).

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Brionac, Dragon of the Ice Barrier). No period ruling in the corpus settles a claimed difference, so the functional call stands unchanged (`unresolved` at both snapshots); the search is recorded in the check. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of Duelist Saga (DUSA-EN073), the first printing carrying the errata'd text Independently corroborated by Konami's own errata announcement and the archived Forbidden & Limited List page carrying its effective date; the printing remains the anchor because it is when the text first became available in the TCG (the announcement and the F/L effective date differ by a few days).

event.historical_text: 1 Tuner + 1 or more non-Tuner monstersYou can discard any number of cards to the Graveyard to target the same number of cards on the field; return those targets to the hand.
event.modern_text: 1 Tuner + 1 or more non-Tuner monstersYou can discard any number of cards to the Graveyard, then target the same number of cards your opponent controls; return those cards to the hand. You can only use this effect of "Brionac, Dragon of the Ice Barrier" once per turn.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the discard-to-bounce Ignition effect gained a hard once per turn (modern e1:SetCountLimit(1,id); the historical script sets no count limit, so it can be used repeatedly in a turn) and its targets were narrowed to the opponent's side - modern Duel.SelectTarget(tp,Card.IsAbleToHand,tp,0,LOCATION_ONFIELD,...) against the historical tp,LOCATION_ONFIELD,LOCATION_ONFIELD, which reaches either player's field. The discard remains a cost in both (historical Duel.SendtoGrave(cg,REASON_COST+REASON_DISCARD) inside the cost function).

rulings_check.difference: Era: the discard-to-bounce effect has no once-per-turn limit and can be used repeatedly in a turn. Modern: hard once per turn ('You can only use this effect of "Brionac, Dragon of the Ice Barrier" once per turn'). Era: the effect returns 'the same number of cards from the field', so it can target cards on either player's side of the field. Modern: only cards the opponent controls.
